paper_metadata.title: Entanglement scaling in matrix product state representation of smooth functions and their shallow quantum circuit approximations

summary: The paper derives rigorous scaling results for entanglement in matrix-product-state (MPS) representations of smooth functions and translates them into shallow linear-depth quantum circuits for state preparation, with application to heavy-tailed financial distributions (alpha-stable / Levy). Using Tensor Cross Interpolation, the authors construct utility-scale encoding circuits and execute them on IBM quantum devices at up to 64 qubits, validating fidelity of the prepared distributions against analytical benchmarks.

experiments.description: MPS-based shallow state preparation of heavy-tailed finance distributions (Levy / alpha-stable), constructed via Tensor Cross Interpolation and compiled to an O(N)-gate quantum circuit, executed on IBM superconducting hardware up to 64 qubits.

algorithm.variant: MPS-to-circuit state preparation with Tensor Cross Interpolation (TCI) + isometry compilation
algorithm.ansatz: linear-depth staircase of two-qubit isometries derived from low-rank MPS approximation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical 1D real / complex function f(x) on [0,1] encoded as amplitudes of an N-qubit state via binary discretization x = sum sigma_i 2^-i; MPS approximation of the resulting rank-N tensor compiled to a circuit of shallow gates.

dataset_specification.description: Target probability distributions used in quantitative finance for modelling heavy-tailed returns, including Levy(mu, c) distributions; additional validation on smooth test functions from the analytical theory.

results.notes: Paper reports fidelity / KL divergence between the prepared state and target smooth / Levy distributions; exact numeric value requires reading the figures (not reproduced here). The authors report that the TCI-based MPS circuits substantially outperform prior MPS encoding schemes at matched bond dimension.

classical_baselines.notes: TCI + improved isometry compilation yields higher fidelity at same bond dimension.
classical_baselines.method_name: Prior MPS-based encoding schemes (refs [9-14, 21-26] in paper)

speedup_claims.magnitude: linear O(N) gate-count state preparation versus O(2^N) naive amplitude encoding
speedup_claims.notes: Gate-count advantage for smooth distributions; relies on the MPS bond dimension remaining small, which the paper proves analytically for smooth functions.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(N) two-qubit gates for bounded-bond MPS encoding.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N * chi^3) for TCI construction of the MPS; O(2^N) for exact amplitude encoding of arbitrary functions.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Expected to survive noise on current IBM devices for smooth heavy-tailed distributions up to ~64 qubits; fault tolerance not required for the encoding step itself.

notes: 64-qubit IBM hardware run read from abstract / introduction; detailed fidelity numerics appear in figures not reproduced in the extracted text.
